abstract: Quantum logic decomposition refers to decomposing a given quantum gate to a set of physically implementable gates. An approach has been presented to decompose arbitrary diagonal quantum gates to a set of multiplexed-rotation gates around $z$ axis. In this paper, a special class of diagonal quantum gates, namely diagonal Hermitian quantum gates, is considered and a new perspective to the decomposition problem with respect to decomposing these gates is presented. It is first shown that these gates can be decomposed to a set that solely consists of multiple-controlled $Z$ gates. Then a binary representation for the diagonal Hermitian gates is introduced. It is shown that the binary representations of multiple-controlled $Z$ gates form a basis for the vector space that is produced by the binary representations of all diagonal Hermitian quantum gates. Moreover, the problem of decomposing a given diagonal Hermitian gate is mapped to the problem of writing its binary representation in the specific basis mentioned above. Moreover, CZ gate is suggested to be the two-qubit gate in the decomposition library, instead of previously used CNOT gate. Experimental results show that the proposed approach can lead to circuits with lower costs in comparison with the previous ones. Keywords— Diagonal Hermitian quantum gates, Optimization, Decomposition

specification.problem: Decompose an n-qubit diagonal Hermitian quantum gate D (a diagonal unitary with all diagonal entries in {+1,-1}) into a product of multiple-controlled Z gates (Z, CZ, CCZ, ...), by mapping D to a binary vector over GF(2) and expressing that vector in the basis formed by the binary representations of the multiple-controlled Z gates.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Scoped to: (i) the characterization of diagonal Hermitian gates as D = sum_x (-1)^{f(x)} |x><x| with a Boolean function f, (ii) a binary (GF(2)) representation of such gates in which gate multiplication becomes XOR, (iii) the fact that the multiple-controlled Z gates correspond to the monomial (algebraic-normal-form) basis of Boolean functions, (iv) the resulting exact decomposition via Mobius inversion, and (v) one tiny explicit instance (n = 2, D = diag(1,-1,-1,-1) = Z_1 Z_2 CZ_{12}). Outside scope: the paper's exact definition/encoding conventions for the binary representation, the further decomposition of multiple-controlled Z gates into the CZ-plus-single-qubit library, the cost model, the optimization procedure, and the reported experimental cost comparisons against prior multiplexed-R_z decompositions.

symbols.meaning: number of qubits acted on by the diagonal gate
computational-basis bit string; qubit 1 is the most significant bit, integer index idx(x)=\sum_{i=1}^{n} x_i 2^{n-i}
diagonal Hermitian (hence also unitary, D^2=I) gate to be decomposed
Boolean function encoding the signs of D, d_x=(-1)^{f(x)}
binary representation of D: the truth table of f as a vector
subset of qubit indices on which a multiple-controlled Z gate acts (|S|=1: Z, |S|=2: CZ, |S|=3: CCZ, ...)
multiple-controlled Z gate applying phase -1 exactly when all qubits in S are 1
monomial Boolean function m_S(x)=\prod_{i\in S}x_i (m_\emptyset\equiv 1); binary representation of C^{S}Z
coefficient of m_S in the GF(2) expansion of f (algebraic normal form coefficient)
bit string with x_i=1 for i\in T and x_i=0 otherwise

equations.label: Diagonal Hermitian gate as a sign function
equations.description: A diagonal gate that is both unitary and Hermitian has real diagonal entries of modulus 1, i.e. each entry is +1 or -1, so it is fully specified by a Boolean function f.
equations.abstract_quote: a special class of diagonal quantum gates, namely diagonal Hermitian quantum gates
equations.justification: Diagonal unitary entries have |d_x|=1; Hermiticity forces d_x real; hence d_x in {+1,-1} and d_x=(-1)^{f(x)}.
assumptions: Gates are considered as exact matrices; global phase is tracked separately via the constant term (see eq_4).

equations.label: Binary representation and its homomorphism property
equations.description: The binary representation is the truth table of f indexed by idx(x). Because (-1)^{f_1(x)}(-1)^{f_2(x)}=(-1)^{f_1(x)\oplus f_2(x)}, multiplying diagonal Hermitian gates corresponds to XOR of their binary representations, giving a GF(2) vector space.
equations.abstract_quote: a binary representation for the diagonal Hermitian gates is introduced
equations.justification: The abstract introduces a binary representation forming a vector space; the natural choice consistent with eq_1 is the truth table of f with XOR as addition. The paper's exact indexing convention is not given, so the idx(x) ordering above is a stated convention.
assumptions: Truth-table encoding with qubit 1 as most significant bit is a chosen convention, not sourced from the abstract.

equations.label: Multiple-controlled Z gate and its binary representation
equations.latex: C^{S}Z=\sum_{x}(-1)^{\prod_{i\in S}x_i}|x\rangle\langle x|=I-2\,|1_S\rangle\langle 1_S|\otimes I_{[n]\setminus S},\qquad b(C^{S}Z)=m_S,\;\; m_S(x)=\prod_{i\in S}x_i
equations.description: C^{S}Z applies -1 exactly when all qubits in S equal 1; its binary representation is the monomial m_S. S={i} gives Z_i, S={i,j} gives CZ_{ij}, |S|=3 gives CCZ.
equations.justification: Standard definition of multiple-controlled Z gates; they are symmetric in control/target so only the set S matters.

equations.label: Monomials form a GF(2) basis (expansion of f)
equations.description: Every Boolean function has a unique algebraic normal form over GF(2); the 2^n monomials are linearly independent and span the space of all binary representations. The nonempty-S monomials are the binary representations of the multiple-controlled Z gates; S=empty corresponds to the global phase -I.
equations.abstract_quote: the binary representations of multiple-controlled $Z$ gates form a basis for the vector space that is produced by the binary representations of all diagonal Hermitian quantum gates
equations.justification: The abstract states the basis property; the ANF/monomial basis is the standard realization of it given eq_2 and eq_3.
assumptions: The constant monomial m_empty (global phase -I) is either included as a trivial 'zero-controlled Z' element or the decomposition is taken up to global phase; the abstract does not say which.

equations.label: Coefficient extraction (Mobius inversion over GF(2))
equations.description: Exact formula for the unique ANF coefficients: a_S is the XOR of f over all bit strings whose support is a subset of S. Equivalent to solving the linear system over GF(2) for the coordinates of b(D) in the monomial basis.
equations.justification: Standard Mobius transform for the algebraic normal form of Boolean functions; computable in O(n 2^n) XOR operations via the fast transform.

equations.label: Decomposition of D into multiple-controlled Z gates
equations.latex: D=(-1)^{a_\emptyset}\prod_{\emptyset\neq S\subseteq[n],\ a_S=1}C^{S}Z\qquad(\text{exact equality; factors commute})
equations.description: Writing b(D) in the monomial basis (eq_4, eq_5) and mapping back through eq_2 and eq_3 yields D exactly as a product of the multiple-controlled Z gates whose coefficient a_S equals 1, times a global sign.
equations.abstract_quote: the problem of decomposing a given diagonal Hermitian gate is mapped to the problem of writing its binary representation in the specific basis mentioned above
equations.justification: Direct consequence of eq_2 (products map to XOR), eq_3 (basis elements are C^S Z) and eq_4; all factors are diagonal so order is irrelevant.
assumptions: Gate count equals the Hamming weight of (a_S)_{S\neq\emptyset}; whether the paper further optimizes beyond this unique expansion (e.g. via the CZ-based library) is not determinable from the abstract.

equations.label: Tiny explicit instance (n = 2)
equations.description: Truth table f(00)=0, f(01)=1, f(10)=1, f(11)=1. Mobius inversion gives all three nonconstant coefficients equal to 1, so D = Z on qubit 1, Z on qubit 2, and CZ on both. Check: diag(1,-1,-1,1) * diag(1,1,1,-1) = diag(1,-1,-1,-1).
equations.justification: Chosen as the smallest instance in which all three two-qubit basis elements appear; verified by direct matrix multiplication of 4x4 diagonals.
assumptions: Instance chosen by the reconstructor; not taken from the paper.

registers.name: q
registers.role: data register on which the diagonal Hermitian gate D acts; qubit 1 is the most significant bit of the index idx(x)

steps.description: Read the Boolean sign function f from the diagonal of D: f(x)=0 if d_x=+1 and f(x)=1 if d_x=-1; form the binary representation b(D).
Classically compute the GF(2) coordinates a_S of b(D) in the monomial basis by Mobius inversion (fast XOR transform).
Emit one multiple-controlled Z gate C^{S}Z for every nonempty S with a_S=1 (in any order, since all factors are diagonal); record a_empty as a global sign.
Instance: for D=diag(1,-1,-1,-1) on 2 qubits, emit Z_1, Z_2, CZ_{12}.

specification.classical_postprocessing: The entire decomposition is classical preprocessing: computing the ANF coefficients a_S of the truth table of f (eq_5) and emitting the corresponding gate list (eq_6). No quantum measurement or quantum postprocessing is involved; correctness can be checked classically by multiplying the emitted diagonal matrices.
assumptions: Binary representation is taken to be the truth table of f over GF(2) with qubit 1 as the most significant bit; the paper's exact encoding may differ.
Global phase (-I, the empty monomial) is tracked as a sign and not realized as a gate.
The decomposition in eq_6 is the unique ANF expansion; any further cost optimization or alternative choice of representatives in the paper is not reconstructed.
Instance n=2, D=diag(1,-1,-1,-1) chosen by the reconstructor as the smallest useful example.
